raw_case_text:
A 52-year-old man with Type 2 diabetes presented with fever, arthralgia, and myalgia for three days after working in paddy fields. On admission, he was febrile, icteric, dyspneic, and hypotensive (blood pressure 93/60 mmHg), with bibasal lung crepitations. He had not urinated for over 6 hours.
Initial tests indicated neutrophilic leukocytosis, severe thrombocytopenia, and elevated liver enzymes and serum creatinine (Table 2). Arterial blood gas analysis showed hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis with a lactate level of 7.1 mmol/L. Chest radiograph suggested severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome. Leptospira MAT was positive at a titer of 1 : 640.
After fluid resuscitation noradrenaline was initiated, the patient was transferred to the ICU. He was electively intubated due to severe hypoxemia. Intravenous ceftriaxone was commenced. Renal replacement therapy by continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration was commenced, and multiple platelet concentrates were given to correct thrombocytopenia. Once stabilized, intermittent hemodialysis was initiated.
On Day 13, the patient developed blood-stained nasogastric aspirate and significant anemia. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed gastric erosions. Anemia was corrected with multiple blood transfusions. The patient was gradually improving by this time with no fever and minimum ventilator support until Day 15, when abdominal tenderness and sluggish bowel sounds were detected. There was intolerance of nasogastric feeds and melena. The abdomen was distended, and an anteroposterior radiograph (Figure 3) showed dilated multiple small bowel loops, a collapsed large bowel but no free gas in the peritoneal cavity. An ultrasound scan confirmed small bowel obstruction. The patient was hemodynamically unstable for contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography scan or for any surgical intervention. He succumbed on Day 21 of illness.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 52-year-old male with diabetes presenting with a 3-day history of fever, arthralgia, and myalgia following work in paddy fields.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 3 days prior to admission following labor in agricultural paddy fields, characterized by acute fever, arthralgias, and generalized myalgias. He was anuric for over 6 hours prior to hospital arrival. In the hospital, he rapidly deteriorated into severe hypoxemia, lactic acidosis, and hypotensive shock requiring endotracheal intubation, vasoactive agents, and continuous renal replacement therapy. On day 13, he developed blood-stained nasogastric aspirate and anemia. On day 15, he developed acute abdominal distension, sluggish bowel sounds, feed intolerance, and melena.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Epidemiological exposure: occupational exposure working in agricultural paddy fields.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports fever, arthralgias, generalized myalgias, anuria, blood-stained nasogastric aspirate, and melena. Home medications: not documented. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Upon admission: febrile, deeply icteric, tachypneic/dyspneic, and hypotensive (blood pressure 93/60 mmHg). Respiratory: bibasal lung crepitations auscultated. Renal: anuria (>6 hours without urine). On day 15: distended abdomen with diffuse tenderness and sluggish/hypoactive bowel sounds.
objective.routine_investigations: Arterial blood gas: severe hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis with serum lactate of 7.1 mmol/L. Complete blood count: neutrophilic leukocytosis, severe thrombocytopenia, and subsequent severe anemia on day 13. Biochemistry: marked elevation in serum creatinine (acute renal failure) and elevated liver transaminases. Chest radiograph: severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome. Abdominal radiograph (anteroposterior): dilated multiple small bowel loops with collapsed large bowel, without pneumoperitoneum. Bedside abdominal ultrasound: confirmed mechanical small bowel obstruction.
objective.advanced_workup: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: multiple gastric mucosal erosions. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT and emergency laparotomy were deferred due to extreme hemodynamic instability.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe leptospirosis (Weil's disease) confirmed by Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) positive at a titer of 1:640. Complex presentation included severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome, severe lactic acidosis (7.1 mmol/L), septic shock, anuric acute kidney injury requiring continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF) and intermittent hemodialysis, severe thrombocytopenia, gastric stress erosions, and acute mesenteric ischemia resulting in small bowel obstruction.
Plan & Treatment: Intravenous fluid resuscitation, noradrenaline infusion; IV ceftriaxone; elective endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation; continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF) transitioned to intermittent hemodialysis; multiple platelet concentrate transfusions; packed red blood cell transfusions for acute anemia.
Outcome: Patient was hemodynamically unstable for surgical exploration or advanced CT angiography; condition deteriorated inexorably, and he succumbed on Day 21 of illness due to multiorgan failure.
